title: TCP listener input plugin creating log spam filling up disk in few (2 - 3 hours)
body:
We encountered a problem where the file descriptor (FD) limit of Fluent Bit was reached, and as a result, we started observing a massive influx of error logs, particularly from the TCP input plugin. We suspect that Fluent Bit began generating an increasing number of file descriptors because the component responsible for accepting the data(at port 5001, which what we have configured in output plugin) was either not functioning or stuck in some way.


We first saw these below logs started coming when FD limit was reached. **During this time TCP input plugin was not used.**

Apr 14 06:25:22 vm4 td-agent-bit[16481]: [2023/04/14 06:25:22] [error] [output:forward:forward.1] no upstream connections available
Apr 14 06:25:22 vm4 td-agent-bit[16481]: [2023/04/14 06:25:22] [error] [net] coult not create client socket, retrying
Apr 14 06:25:22 vm4 td-agent-bit[16481]: [2023/04/14 06:25:22] [error] [output:forward:forward.1] no upstream connections available
Apr 14 06:25:22 vm4 td-agent-bit[16481]: [2023/04/14 06:25:22] [error] [net] coult not create client socket, retrying
Apr 14 06:25:22 vm4 td-agent-bit[16481]: [2023/04/14 06:25:22] [error] [output:forward:forward.1] no upstream connections available

Apr 14 06:25:22 vm4 td-agent-bit[16481]: [2023/04/14 06:25:22] [  Error] timerfd: Too many open files, errno=24 at /tmp/fluent-bit/lib/monkey/mk_core/mk_event_epoll.c:208
Apr 14 06:25:22 vm4 td-agent-bit[16481]: [2023/04/14 06:25:22] [error] [sched]  'retry request' could not be created. the system might be running out of memory or file descriptors.
Apr 14 06:25:22 vm4 td-agent-bit[16481]: [2023/04/14 06:25:22] [ warn] [engine] retry for chunk '16481-1681453518.322193481.flb' could not be scheduled: input=tail.1 > output=forward.1

**These logs were coming regularly but rate of these logs was acceptable.**
Later when FD limit was already breached and someone tried to connect to TCP input plugin we saw millions of logs error coming because of TCP input plugin. 
Apr 13 17:46:17 vm4 td-agent-bit[4856]: accept4: Too many open files
 Apr 13 17:46:17 vm4 td-agent-bit[4856]: [2023/04/13 17:46:17] [error] [input:tcp:listener] could not accept new connection
 Apr 13 17:46:17 vm4 td-agent-bit[4856]: accept4: Too many open files
 Apr 13 17:46:17 vm4 td-agent-bit[4856]: [2023/04/13 17:46:17] [error] [input:tcp:listener] could not accept new connection

Anybody aware why tcp input plugin is emitting millions of logs of same type? is there any way to limit these logs...its causing OS disk full issue.

Increasing the limit of FD might not work here as ideally our service dont use that many FD....we only reach FD limit when the component accepting the data is not working or stuck. So may be that's the reason fluent bit tries to open more and more socket inorder to preserve data in TCP buffers and hence increasing file descriptors.

My main ask here is how do I limit these error logs from TCP input plugin as these are coming very frequently and keep on coming and filling up whole disk space within 2 - 3 hours.

We should see how we can minimize the millions of logs to a way more less error logging when this scenario hits.

We should also see why the TCP input plugin is attempting to reconnect(trying to make socket FD in this case) in a very tight loop? Is there a parameter available to configure the retry interval for the TCP input plugin? Currently, it appears to retry immediately and continue trying, resulting in high CPU usage.

** To reproduce high rate of error logs from TCP input plugin follow below step:**

Checking the current soft and hard limit of FDs for td-agent-bit:

Now check the current FDs used by td-agent-bit:

Now set the softlimit and hardlimit of td-agent-bit to “current FD usage” + 3

Now run: “sudo systemctl daemon-reload” and then run “sudo systemctl restart td-agent-bit.service”

Again check the soft and hard limit using cmd “prlimit -p <PID> --nofile” …it should be equal to what you have set.

Open another terminal for same VM and run a script which try to send logs to tail input plugin at high rate.

Now you can check the FD usage of td-agent-bit, it should have reached the limit you have set.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
You have an error here and you potentially will lose data so reporting that is vital I think.
Ultimately resolving the underlying error should be the priority, I think anything else is just hiding failures. You need to tune your buffering and retries to cope with what you want to do during your outage.

Logs should always be rotating and [using a separate partition](https://<redacted-host>/examples/guide-checklist.html#xccdf_org.ssgproject.content_group_configure_auditd_data_retention) as well for best practice to prevent this kind of issue with any tool.

Saying that, a state-based error report limited to "we're now in an error state" and indicated that via metrics too would be nice. There is the recent log suppression functionality too although that's only recently introduced and will reduce rather than remove logs entirely.

I think something was asked on Slack too around this: https://<redacted-host>/archives/C0CTQGHKJ/p1683701639201519
In that I indicated how to potentially resolve the logging issue via the [systemd unit approach](https://serverfault.com/a/858845). However, I'll say again: there is an error that will cause you problems potentially and just hiding it is not the best idea.

There are also ways to not log things, e.g. use `log_level off` in the output plugin, but then you lose all information.

And finally, please follow the issue template - there's a lot of missing information here, e.g. config, version used, OS, etc. that should all be captured to help diagnose issues.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: I think the request here is a state/event based logging approach as a feature request, potentially log suppress can help already but that is not documented yet.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
Fluent-bit doesn't deliberately keep connections open to hold data in the connection buffer. It does however not forcefully close inactive connections so the clients sending that data might be just not properly closing the connections (which is a common error) which means those will only be closed when the kernel decides to according to the systems configuration.

There is a setting named `net.io_timeout` which you could set to a reasonable value in order to terminate those dangling connections.

There's also `net.accept_timeout_log_error` which you can set to `off` which will silence those `[2023/04/13 17:46:17] [error] [input:tcp:listener] could not accept new connection` but not the `accept4: Too many open files` because the later is not emitted through the fluent-bit logging pipeline but rather directly printed to `stderr` using `perror`.

So you  can either set [log_file](https://<redacted-host>/manual/administration/configuring-fluent-bit/classic-mode/configuration-file) in fluent-bit to save those logs directly to a file or do something to ignore `stderr` in your host but that's not something I can make any comments on.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Did you try redirecting stderr (and stdout) to prevent the log from filling up?
As you're using systemd in your Slack message then use the link I provided above to show you, that's a standard feature of systemd: `StandardError=null` / `StandardOutput=null`

`accept4: Too many open files` is an error reported by system libraries so redirecting stderr will hide it - Leo indicated this above in that it does not come from Fluent Bit but directly via `perror`.

I'm not going to say this is a good idea or recommend it.

The logs are legitimately reporting errors but I appreciate it may be at a high rate and there is no good solution currently that will reduce that rate other than resolving the error.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
@participant2 :  There seems to be some missing context. Most of the file descriptors were being consumed by another output plugin because the destination was not reading the data. This particular output plugin was receiving data from other Tail input plugins we have. I believe this led to the fluent bit output plugin creating more and more sockets (file descriptors), eventually reaching the file descriptor limit for fluent bit. It's important to note that during this time, the TCP input plugin was not even being used.

Once the file descriptor limit is reached, if a client tries to connect to the TCP input plugin, it starts generating these log messages indefinitely, even when the client has stopped attempting to connect to the TCP input plugin.

The configuration setting you provided is for the TCP input plugin. However, it is not relevant to the issue until the file descriptor limit is reached.

Output plugin:
[OUTPUT]
    Name       forward
    Host       127.0.0.1
    Port       5001
    Match      azure*

Additionally, I couldn't find the "net.io_timeout" setting in the official documentation ?

Also could you pls reopen the issue, as it is not resolved yet.
